symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers, a count of bits.
symbols.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each of the two input integers; here $n$ counts bits, not the sequence entries used on the convolution page.

symbols.name: lower-bound constant
symbols.meaning: A positive constant, depending on the machine A, in its eventual lower bound.
symbols.quote: For a fixed machine $A$, let $c_A$ be a positive constant and $N_A$ the input length from which the bound holds.

symbols.name: bound threshold
symbols.meaning: The input length from which the eventual lower bound for machine A holds.
symbols.quote: For a fixed machine $A$, let $c_A$ be a positive constant and $N_A$ the input length from which the bound holds.

symbols.name: base-2 logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm, so that $\lg n$ stands for $\log_2 n$.
symbols.quote: Write $\lg n$ for $\log_2 n$, and take $\log=\log_2$ in $n\log n$; another base only multiplies $n \log n$ by a constant, which changes none of the claims below.

relations.quote: In this model the lower-bound question is settled by the [limit inferior](limit-inferior.md) of the ratio $T_A(n)/(n\log n)$.
Costs in this model are measured against [Schönhage–Strassen multiplication](schonhage-strassen.md).
This model restricts [the n log n optimality conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) to one machine at a time.
